items.title: William Russell Interview, 1976-02-16
items.q: in the early records I made, sometimes Bunk and Jim Robinson would play a good deal together

ctx.x: How did they see him? Did they see him as a proponent of the... I mean, as a representative of the pure New Orleans style? Did they even know that that existed? Well, ordinarily, the people that would go in there just to dance wouldn't even know or care too much. But the press, I mean, how would they talk about him?

Yeah, they played up the New Orleans angle a good deal, and the fact that his age and all, he wasn't really that old. He died before he was 70. And when you say, look at some place like Preservation Hall, people that are going there in their 70s, Jim Robinson at 85 now, as good as he ever was, practically, maybe not quite as much lung power or powerful, and he can't dance quite like he used to, but he gets along all right at 85. He may only be 83, actually.
Or he may be 93. No, I don't think he's 93, but I mean, you know.

items.title: William Russell Interview, 1975-02-02
items.q: And I'd suggested that, uh, Woody Brune had used, uh, people like Piku and, uh, Big Eye Louie, uh, and, uh, mentioned that Jim Robinson to him.

ctx.x: The, uh, same studio. I'd have to look that up. I looked all that up for Ralph Gleason about, uh, two or three months ago. Ralph had had the idea it was WWL. It wasn't that. Uh, that, uh, that Bunk had made his records for Jean Williams. Jean did make some records at a studio, WSMB, I guess. His—I know, WSMB, in the Maison Blanc's building in 1942. Uh, Woody, uh, I'm not real sure. I don't have the dope at hand right now. It might have been W—WL, which is the Roosevelt Hotel, possibly, at that time. But, uh,…
Well, he probably hadn't lived here since 1918, I guess.
